mainTopic: When בית דין may and may not add a leap month (עיבור השנה): famine, timing around ראש השנה, שביעית, and טומאה
overview: This amud deals with when בית דין may add an extra month to the year (עיבור השנה), and when it may not. It opens with the rule that we do not add a month in years of famine, and proves it from אלישע. Even in בעל שלישה, the fastest-ripening place, only barley was ripe after the עומר, yet אלישע did not add a month because people were hungry. Next, a ברייתא rules that a leap year may not be set before ראש השנה. A coded letter sent to רבא seems to show the Sages doing it in אב, and the answer is that they may calculate early but may not announce it. The גמרא then shows from שלמה's officers that the code word נציב means a month. More limits follow: no deciding a year ahead, no three leap years in a row (the story of רבי עקיבא in prison is pushed aside), and no leap year in שביעית or the year after, where בית רבן גמליאל disagreed. The amud ends with a dispute about adding a month because of טומאה, where רבי יהודה brings the story of חזקיה. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No leap year during years of famine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from the previous daf finishes its list: we do not add a month to the year in years of famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: (We do not make the year a leap year) during years of famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from the previous daf of times when בית דין does not add an extra month to the year. The last item is years of famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a month pushes the עומר later. Until the עומר is brought, the new grain may not be eaten. In a famine, that delay would leave people hungry even longer.

keyTerms.meaning: years of famine
making the year a leap year by adding a month
the extra month added in a leap year

phrases.english: during years of famine.
phrases.notes: This is the last item of a list that began on the previous daf: times when we don't add a month to the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from the previous daf about when not to make a leap year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year is not declared during years of famine.

steps.title: רבי quotes the story of the man from בעל שלישה
steps.stepSummary: רבי brings a פסוק about a man who brought אלישע barley loaves of first fruits, as a proof for the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: "And a man came from בעל שלישה and brought the man of God bread of the first fruits, twenty loaves of barley..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי quotes a פסוק about אלישע. This sets up a proof that will be explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, the פסוק just tells a story. רבי will read its details closely (the place, the kind of grain, the timing) to show that אלישע chose not to add a month because of famine.

keyTerms.meaning: it is taught (in a ברייתא)
a place in ארץ ישראל known for very early crops
the man of God, meaning the prophet אלישע
bread made from the first fruits to ripen

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: "And a man came from Baal Shalishah
and he brought to the man of God
bread of the first fruits,
twenty loaves of barley, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a scriptural story to support the rule that we don't make a leap year in famine.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a leap year is not declared in years of famine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 4:42, the man from בעל שלישה who brought אלישע barley loaves.

steps.title: Even in the fastest-ripening place, only one crop was ready
steps.stepSummary: בעל שלישה ripens its crops earlier than anywhere else, yet only one kind of grain had ripened.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no place in all of ארץ ישראל where fruit ripens faster than בעל שלישה, and even so, only one kind had ripened.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי starts explaining the פסוק. Even in the place with the earliest crops, only one species was ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even בעל שלישה had only one ripe crop, then the rest of the country was even further behind. That means the season was late, which is a sign that the year needed an extra month.

keyTerms.meaning: quick, fast (here: quick to ripen)
to ripen its produce
even so
one species

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ קַלָּה בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: And there is no place in all of Eretz Yisrael quicker
to ripen its fruits
than Baal Shalishah,
and even so,
only one species had ripened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ קַלָּה בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the place named in the פסוק to show the crops were late.
steps.raayaObject: That the crops that year were behind schedule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The mention of בעל שלישה and of "first fruits" in the פסוק.

steps.title: It was barley, and it was after the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק shows the grain was barley, not wheat, and that the story happened after the עומר was brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you will say it was wheat? The פסוק says "barley." Perhaps you will say it was before the עומר? The פסוק says "Give to the people and let them eat." So it was after the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rules out two wrong ways to read the story, using words from the פסוק itself. He shows it was barley, and that it was after the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat ripens after barley, close to שבועות, so ripe wheat would mean the season was well along, not late. Before the עומר, unripe crops would be normal. But it was barley, after the עומר, and still only barley was ripe, so the season really was behind.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps you will say
the verse teaches (by saying)
the barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits the new grain
wheat

steps.confusionAlert: Barley ripening is not the problem here. Barley is supposed to be ripe by the עומר. The problem is that nothing besides barley was ripe, even in the fastest place in the country.

phrases.english: Perhaps you will say: wheat?
The verse teaches: "barley."
Perhaps you will say: before the omer?
The verse teaches: "Give to the people and let them eat."
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק. New grain may not be eaten before the עומר, so eating means the עומר was already brought.

phrases.english: It was after the omer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the proof by ruling out readings that would weaken it.
steps.raayaObject: That the late ripening was real: only barley was ready, even after the עומר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words "barley" and "Give to the people and let them eat" in the פסוק.

steps.title: The year deserved a leap month, but famine stopped אלישע
steps.stepSummary: The year should have been a leap year, but אלישע did not add a month because it was a year of famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: So now we can say: that year was fit to be made a leap year. Why didn't אלישע make it one? Because it was a year of shortage, and everyone was running to the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי draws the conclusion. The year needed an extra month, but אלישע skipped it because of the famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 4 showed that the crops were late, which is a normal reason to add a month. אלישע still did not add one, because a later עומר would keep the new grain forbidden longer while people were starving. This proves the rule from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: now you can say (introducing the conclusion)
fit to be made a leap year
a year of shortage or drought
the threshing floors, where grain is gathered

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the crops are late and a leap month is called for, בית דין does not add one in a famine year, because it would delay the עומר and keep the new grain forbidden longer. אלישע acted this way in the story of בעל שלישה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the needs of the people can override the normal reasons for making a leap year.

phrases.english: Say from now:
that year was fit to be made a leap year,
and why did Elisha not make it a leap year?
Because it was a year of shortage,
and everyone was running to the threshing floors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the details of the פסוק and ties it back to the rule in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The year deserved a leap month, but אלישע did not add one because of the famine, which proves that a leap year is not declared in years of famine.

steps.title: No leap year before ראש השנה; in an emergency, right after
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a leap year cannot be declared before ראש השנה. In an emergency it may be declared right after ראש השנה, but only by adding a second אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We do not make a leap year before ראש השנה, and if the court did, it does not count. But because of pressing need, the court may make it a leap year right after ראש השנה. Even so, the added month must be a second אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the earliest time a court may decide to make the coming year a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three rules here. Before ראש השנה, a leap-year decision does not work at all. Right after ראש השנה it is allowed only in an emergency, and even then the added month is always a second אדר, never some other month.

keyTerms.meaning: We make the year a leap year by adding a month
A year that has become a leap year
Because of pressing need, an emergency
The month that gets doubled in a leap year

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We do not make the year a leap year
before Rosh HaShana,
and if they did make it a leap year, it is not a leap year.
But because of pressing need

phrases.aramaic: מְעַבְּרִין אוֹתָהּ אַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִיָּד,
phrases.english: they may make it a leap year immediately after Rosh HaShana,
and even so
they add only an extra Adar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the timing of the leap-year decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year may not be declared before ראש השנה. In an emergency it may be declared right after ראש השנה, but only by adding a second אדר.

steps.title: A coded letter to רבא: two messengers were caught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge by quoting a coded letter sent to רבא. This first part reports that two scholars were caught by the Romans while carrying תכלת, and that they escaped alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But they sent a message to רבא: 'A pair came from רקת, and an eagle caught them, and they were carrying things made in לוז.' (What were these things? תכלת.) 'In the merit of mercy and in their own merit, they got out safely.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא and starts quoting a coded letter. This part is background; the real challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Roman persecution, the Sages wrote in code. The two scholars were caught, so they never delivered their message. This explains why a letter had to be sent, and the letter goes on to report the leap-year decision.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening for a challenge
A pair, here two Torah scholars
Eagle, code for the Roman soldiers
A place where תכלת was made
Sky-blue dye used for ציצית

phrases.english: Is that so?
But they sent a message to Rava:
A pair came from Rakkath,
phrases.notes: רקת is an old name for טבריה, where the Sages' court sat at that time.

phrases.english: and an eagle caught them,
phrases.notes: The 'eagle' is code for the Roman soldiers.

phrases.english: and in their hands were things made in Luz.
And what were they? Techeles (sky-blue dye).
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא explaining the code. It is not part of the letter.

phrases.english: In the merit of mercy and in their own merit
they got out in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge to the ברייתא by quoting a historical letter.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a leap year cannot be decided before ראש השנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This part only sets up the letter; the attacking detail comes in the next step.

steps.title: The Sages set up a leap year in the month of Av
steps.stepSummary: The letter continues: the Roman ruler blocked the נשיא's court from adding a month, so the Sages met secretly and decided on a leap year in אב, the month אהרן הכהן died. אב comes before ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The descendants of נחשון wanted to set up one pillar (an extra month), but that Edomite would not let them. But the members of the assembly gathered and set up one pillar in the month in which אהרן הכהן died.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the challenge. The letter reports a leap year decided in אב, which is before ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן died in אב, which comes before ראש השנה. So the Sages decided on a leap year before ראש השנה, which seems to go against the ברייתא's rule that such a decision does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of נחשון, meaning the court of the נשיא
Pillar or officer, code for an extra month
That Edomite, meaning the Roman ruler
Members of the assembly, meaning the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is the Roman ruler. The problem is the timing: אב comes BEFORE ראש השנה, and the ברייתא said a leap year cannot be decided then.

phrases.english: And the ones carried from the thighs of Nachshon
phrases.notes: Code for the court of the נשיא, who came from נחשון's family.

phrases.english: wanted to set up one pillar,
phrases.notes: 'Pillar' is code for adding a month to the year.

phrases.english: but that Edomite did not let them.
But the members of the assembly gathered
and set up one pillar for it
in the month in which Aaron the Kohen died.
phrases.notes: That is the month of אב, before ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲמוּסֵי יְרֵיכֵי נַחְשׁוֹן בִּקְּשׁוּ לִקְבּוֹעַ נְצִיב אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the letter and delivers the actual challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a leap year decided before ראש השנה does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Sages decided on a leap year in אב, before ראש השנה, and treated it as valid.

steps.title: Calculate early, but announce only later
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the court may calculate before ראש השנה that a leap year is needed, but may not announce it until after ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Calculating, they may calculate; announcing, they may not announce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating working out the decision from announcing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אב the Sages only figured out that the coming year needed an extra month. The ברייתא forbids publishing or finalizing the leap year before ראש השנה, so the letter does not contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: They may calculate
They may not reveal or announce

steps.whatToRemember: Before ראש השנה, a court may work out that a leap year is needed, but it may not announce it until after ראש השנה.

phrases.english: To calculate, they may calculate;
to reveal, they do not reveal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the letter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The letter seemed to show a leap year fully decided before ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the calculation was done in אב; the announcement waits until after ראש השנה.

steps.title: How do we know נציב means a month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the code word נציב in the letter means a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see that this word נציב is a word for a month?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the letter's code and asks where the word נציב comes from. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole reading of the letter depended on נציב meaning an added month. The גמרא wants a source for that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we see it?
A word meaning month

phrases.english: From where do we see
that this word 'netziv' is a term for a month?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי נְצִיב לִישָּׁנָא דְּיַרְחָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to explain a code word used in the letter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that נציב refers to a month

steps.title: Solomon's twelve officers, one for each month
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says שלמה had twelve officers who each supplied the king for one month a year, so a נציב is tied to a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And שלמה had twelve officers over all Israel, and they provided for the king and his men, a month in the year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that links each officer, a נציב, to one month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twelve officers, each in charge of one month, means each נציב stands for a month. That is why the letter could use נציב as code for an added month.

keyTerms.meaning: Officers
And they provided food and supplies

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And Solomon had twelve officers
over all Israel,
and they provided for the king and his men
a month in the year."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word נציב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שלמה's twelve נציבים each served one month, so נציב is linked to a month.

steps.title: But the פסוק mentions one more officer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a later פסוק mentions another officer 'in the land,' which seems to make more than twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'And one officer that was in the land'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with the פסוק it just quoted: there seems to be an extra officer beyond the twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there were twelve officers for twelve months, who was this extra one? That seems to break the neat one-officer-per-month picture.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written?
One officer that was in the land

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And one officer that was in the land"?
phrases.notes: מלכים א 4:19. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, filling in the פסוק fully.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of officers in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The picture of exactly twelve officers, one per month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later פסוק mentions another officer, which seems to make thirteen.

steps.title: The extra officer: a head officer or the leap month
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה and רב נחמן each explain the extra officer. One says he was in charge of all the others; the other says he served in the added leap month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה and רב נחמן: one says he was one officer appointed over all of them, and the other says he was for the leap month.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers about who the extra officer was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first answer, the extra officer was a supervisor over the twelve, not a thirteenth monthly officer. In the second answer, he was in charge of the extra month in a leap year, which fits well with נציב meaning a month.

keyTerms.meaning: One says
Appointed over all of them
The added month of a leap year

steps.whatToRemember: נציב is linked to a month. According to one view, a thirteenth נציב served in the leap month.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda and Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אֶחָד מְמוּנֶּה עַל כּוּלָּם,
phrases.english: one says: one officer was appointed over all of them;
and one says: he matched the leap month.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב נַחְמָן חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra officer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two alternative explanations of the extra officer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra officer seemed to break the one-officer-per-month count.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was either a head officer over the twelve or the officer for the leap month.

steps.title: No leap year decided a year ahead, and not three in a row
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that בית דין may not make a leap year from one year to the next, and may not make three leap years in a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: We do not make a leap year from one year to the next, and we do not make three leap years one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with two limits on making a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first limit is about timing: you cannot settle next year's leap status while still in this year. The second limit is about how often: three leap years in a row is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught; this opens a ברייתא
Making the year a leap year by adding a month
To its fellow, meaning to the next year
One after the other

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not make the year a leap year
not from one year to its fellow,
phrases.notes: This means deciding now, ahead of time, that next year will be a leap year.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ.
phrases.english: and not three years one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה לֹא מִשָּׁנָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of ברייתות about leap year limits after the discussion of the code word נציב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year may not be decided a year in advance, and three leap years in a row are not made.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's story: רבי עקיבא made three leap years in a row
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון brings a story where רבי עקיבא, while in prison, made three leap years one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: There was a story with רבי עקיבא when he was locked in prison, and he made three leap years one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון brings a real story to show that three leap years in a row can happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story seems to go against the second rule of the ברייתא. If a great sage like רבי עקיבא did it, then it should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident used as proof
Locked up, imprisoned
Prison
He made it a leap year

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
There was an incident with Rabbi Akiva
who was locked up in prison,

phrases.aramaic: וְעִיבֵּר שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ.
phrases.english: and he made three years leap years, one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule against three leap years in a row with a story.
steps.raayaObject: That three leap years in a row may be made
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי עקיבא in prison

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: each year was set at its own time
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that רבי עקיבא's story proves nothing, because בית דין set each leap year separately at its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? A court sat and set each one at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push away רבי שמעון's proof from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא only worked out the calculations. The real decision was made by בית דין one year at a time, so it was never a decision made ahead of time. This fits the idea from step 9 that calculating is different from officially setting the year.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there a proof from there? A way of rejecting a proof
They set, officially fixed
At its proper time

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there a proof from there?
A court sat and set
each one at its proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the story, not the story itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story does not show a court deciding three years at once; each year was set separately at its time
steps.whatToRemember: Working out a leap year ahead of time is fine; officially setting it must happen in its own year.

steps.title: No leap year in שביעית or the year after; the usual time is the year before
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a leap year is not made in שביעית or the year after it, and that the usual time is the year before שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: We do not make a leap year in the seventh year or in the year after the seventh year. When do they usually make a leap year? In the year before the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about which years should not be made into leap years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a month in שביעית would make its restrictions last longer. Adding a month in the year after would make people wait longer for the new crop when food is scarce. So the preferred time is the year before שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, when the land rests
The year right after שביעית
Usually, as a regular practice
The year just before שביעית

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: The Sages taught: We do not make the year a leap year
not in the seventh year
and not in the year after the seventh year.
When are they accustomed to make a leap year?
On the eve of the seventh year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה לֹא בִּשְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא adding more limits on when to make a leap year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No leap year in שביעית or the year after; the normal time is the year before שביעית.

steps.title: בית רבן גמליאל made leap years in the year after שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the court of רבן גמליאל did make leap years in the year after שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court of רבן גמליאל would make leap years in the year after the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reports a different practice from בית רבן גמליאל, which goes against the rule just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there are two opinions about the year after שביעית. The first part of the ברייתא forbids it, while בית רבן גמליאל did it. The גמרא will next explain what this disagreement depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: The court of רבן גמליאל

phrases.english: Those of the house of Rabban Gamliel
would make leap years in the year after the seventh year.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיוּ מְעַבְּרִין בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting practice to the rule in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית רבן גמליאל allowed a leap year in the year after שביעית.

steps.title: This matches a dispute about bringing vegetables from outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the leap year disagreement follows a dispute between תנאים about bringing vegetables from חוץ לארץ during שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows the dispute of these תנאים, as it was taught: We do not bring vegetables from outside the Land, and our Rabbis permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the leap year disagreement to another known disagreement about importing vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you may bring vegetables from outside ארץ ישראל, food is less scarce after שביעית. Then adding a month in the year after שביעית is not so hard, which fits בית רבן גמליאל. If you may not bring them in, food is short, so no leap year then.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Vegetables
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And it is in the dispute of these Tannaim,
as it was taught:
We do not bring vegetables from outside the Land,
phrases.notes: This is talking about bringing them in during שביעית.

phrases.english: and our Rabbis permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the disagreement of steps 17 and 18 by linking it to another dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leap year disagreement depends on whether vegetables may be brought from חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: What is the real point of the vegetable dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two sides of the vegetable dispute are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next step: why would anyone forbid bringing vegetables in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave two rulings with no reasons. The גמרא wants to know what point the two sides really disagree on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the two opinions about importing vegetables actually disagree about

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the dispute is about clods of earth
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that the dispute is whether we worry about clods of earth from outside ארץ ישראל stuck to the vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The difference between them is whether we worry about their clods of earth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question by naming the exact point of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earth from חוץ לארץ is treated as impure. The side that forbids worries that bits of that earth will come in on the vegetables. The side that permits does not worry about this.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we worry
Their clods of earth
This is the difference between them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Whether we worry about their clods of earth
phrases.notes: Earth from outside ארץ ישראל is treated as impure, so the worry is dirt stuck to the vegetables.

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְגוּשֵׁיהֶן אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two sides disagree whether to worry about impure clods of earth from חוץ לארץ clinging to the vegetables
steps.whatToRemember: The year after שביעית question ties to food supply, and the food supply question ties to the worry about impure earth from חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: No leap year because of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא rules that בית דין does not make a leap year because of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: We do not make a leap year because of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא with another reason that is not enough for making a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if many people are impure and would like more time to become pure before פסח, this alone is not a reason to add a month.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not make the year a leap year
because of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה מִפְּנֵי הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about reasons that do not justify a leap year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאה is not a reason to make a leap year.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says a leap year may be made because of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא and rules that בית דין may make a leap year because of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They do make a leap year because of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives a second opinion. רבי יהודה says the opposite of the first opinion: בית דין may add a month because of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said בית דין does not make a leap year because of טומאה. רבי יהודה disagrees, so making a leap year for this reason is now an open מחלוקת. The single word מעברין answers the same question with the opposite ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion in this ברייתא
They make a leap year by adding an extra month
Making a leap year by adding a second אדר

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: They do intercalate the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to the ruling of the ברייתא in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, בית דין may make a leap year because of טומאה.

steps.title: The story of חזקיה making a leap year because of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a story: חזקיה מלך יהודה made a leap year because of טומאה, and then asked for mercy for himself, as the פסוק describes people who were not pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a story with חזקיה, king of יהודה, who made a leap year because of טומאה. Then he asked for mercy for himself, as it is written: 'For many of the people, many from אפרים and מנשה, יששכר and זבולון, had not purified themselves.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a story from תנ״ך to show that a leap year really was made because of טומאה. A king of יהודה did exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that חזקיה added a month because the people were impure. The פסוק shows the problem: many people had not become pure. There is a twist, though. חזקיה asked for mercy for himself, which suggests something was not fully right, so the reader should hold onto that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or real event brought as a proof
חזקיה, a righteous king of יהודה
He asked for mercy, meaning he prayed for forgiveness
As it is written; it introduces a פסוק
They had not purified themselves

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at 'he made a leap year, so it is allowed.' The story also says חזקיה asked for mercy for himself. That detail suggests something about what he did needed forgiveness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with Hezekiah, king of Judea,
who intercalated the year because of ritual impurity,
and he asked for mercy for himself,
as it is written: “For a multitude of the people,”
“even many of Ephraim and Manasseh,”
“Issachar and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחִזְקִיָּה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה supports his ruling from step 23 with a story from history.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that a leap year may be made because of טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of חזקיה מלך יהודה, who made a leap year because of טומאה, together with the פסוק in דברי הימים ב 30:18
